name: Dompe
description: Dompe is a popular Philippine survival card game, also known as Knock Poker. It combines poker hand rankings with draw-and-discard mechanics. Players aim to build the best five-card hand and 'knock' (call Dompe) before their opponents, or win instantly with specific six-card combinations.

history.origins: Originating in the Philippines, Dompe is a localized version of Knock Poker. It has been a staple social game in Philippine households and community centers for decades.
timeline: Mid-20th Century: Variations of Knock Poker reach the Philippines and local rules evolve.
1990s: Rules for Dompe are documented in various gaming forums and by card historians like John McLeod.
Modern Era: Remains one of the most popular 'quick' poker variants in the region.
history.cultural: Used as a fast-paced gambling or social game, often played during breaks or community gatherings.
history.evolution: The inclusion of instant-win six-card hands (like three pairs or a sixndcard flush) sets it apart from standard Western Knock Poker.

setup.players: 2 to 5 players using one deck. Additional decks can be added for more players.
setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck plus one Joker (53 tiles).
setup.dealing: 5 cards dealt to each player, one at a time, in an anti-clockwise direction.
setup.equipment: One deck of cards, betting chips (one chip ante per player).

rules.objective: Win the pot by having the best fivendcard poker hand when the round ends, or win instantly with a sixndcard combination.
rules.gameplay:
1. Drawing: Players take turns in anti-clockwise order, drawing the top card from the deck or the last discarded card.
2. Calling Dompe: After drawing, if a player believes they have the best 5-card hand, they call 'Dompe'. This ends the game after the current round concludes.
3. Discarding: After drawing (and potentially calling), the player must discard one card.
keyRules: Anti-clockwise play: Dealing and turns move to the right.
The Joker is wild and can represent any card.
Six-Card Instant Wins: Six-card Flush, Six-card Straight, or Three Pairs win the pot immediately without waiting for a round to end.

strategy.basic: Keep track of the cards being discarded. If you see high-rank suits being dumped, it's safer to go for a straight or a pair than a flush.
strategy.intermediate: Do not call Dompe too early. If you call with two pair, you risk an opponent drawing a third card to beat you in the final round.
strategy.advanced: Bluffing: Call Dompe with a mediocre hand if you suspect your opponents are holding 'junk' and are unlikely to improve in their final turn.
tips: The Joker is your most valuable asset for completing a six-card straight.
If you draw a card that completes three pairs, reveal it immediately for an automated win.
